result.summary: Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that executes Guix builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows, then runs unit and functional test suites against the resulting release binaries on native runners. It realizes the Guix codesign manifest before building to verify codesign environments, exports time-machine metadata for container image caching, and configures test runners dynamically from unpacked release archives.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's exact Guix release binaries and codesigning environments are not continuously tested in CI. Build manifest breakages, missing codesign dependencies, and platform- or toolchain-specific regressions can go undetected until manual release engineering, leaving upcoming toolchain changes such as fully static glibc builds without automated coverage.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently there is limited continuous testing of our exact release binaries... in the event that we start shipping some fully-static Linux builds (x64 and aarch64) as per current revision of #25573, our entire custom-built static glibc and compiler toolchain would be relatively untested by current CI jobs, and that would also be tested here.'
Commit 21ef8cbd18: 'The regular Guix builds do not evaluate the codesign manifest, so missing imports and broken signing dependencies can go unnoticed until signing.'
result.scope_notes: Adds container orchestration scripts, a Guix Dockerfile requiring unprivileged/insecure container capabilities, and an auxiliary Python test runner script that adjusts configuration paths for unpacked binary archives.
result.changed_since_previous: Retains the overall design from the earlier version, updating container scripts and runner test execution steps.
result.card: Adds a GitHub Actions CI workflow that builds Bitcoin Core release packages with Guix for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and runs unit and functional tests on the resulting binaries using native runners. Currently, Guix release binaries and codesigning environments are not continuously built or verified in CI, leaving toolchain bugs and packaging breakages unnoticed until release engineering. The change also validates codesign manifests and provides the necessary CI infrastructure to safely introduce fully static Linux release builds (#25573).

risk.why: Mistakes could break or slow down CI workflows and increase runner resource consumption, but will not affect consensus, runtime node behavior, or released software.
